## TL;DR

Review round 2. The command palette (`SearchOverlay.vue`) is shared by the
header ⌘K pill, the settings palette and the context palette, so the fixes live
in that one component. This round corrects the review's listbox and status
findings, closes the overlapping-load and detached-trigger edge cases, and
keeps focus where the user was after doc, skill and setting results. The
scoped check passed before the round-1 handoff; the round-2 check is rerun
after these changes.

## Work and rationale

- **Listbox children.** The round-1 listbox held the empty and truncated
  messages, which are not valid listbox children. The listbox now wraps only
  options and groups. The empty and loading copy moved into one persistent
  `role="status"` element outside it. Because the element always exists, state
  changes are announced; a status created on demand would not be reliable.
  Truncation text stays a plain sibling.
- **`aria-expanded`.** The reviewer asked for `props.open`. I did not take that
  change. The combobox pattern defines expanded as "the popup is displayed", and
  here the popup is the listbox. While nothing is listed the listbox is not
  rendered, so the combobox reads collapsed and `aria-controls` is omitted. The
  overlay being open is a different state from the popup being shown.
- **Overlapping body loads.** A counter tags each load. Only the newest load may
  clear `loadingBodies`, so an older load settling mid-fetch cannot show "No
  results" while a newer load is still running. A test drives two pending
  fetches and resolves the older one first.
- **Detached trigger.** `lastFocused` can be unmounted by dismiss time. Focus
  now falls back to the header pill (`.search-input`) when the remembered element
  is no longer connected, rather than to `body`.
- **Result focus.** I first passed `null` into the close path for non-task
  results, which would have fallen back to the pill and pulled focus from a task
  drawer. I replaced the nullable argument with an explicit `restoreFocus` flag.
  Task results skip the restore; doc, skill and setting results restore it.
  A caller's `returnFocusEl` still wins in every case.

## Approaches tried

For the status element I considered a `role="status"` node created only when a
message appears. Dynamically inserted live regions are announced unreliably, so
I kept one node that always exists and changes its text.

For the detached-trigger case I considered only checking `isConnected` and
leaving focus on `body`. The header pill is the one global trigger, so falling
back to it keeps keyboard users in the same place.

## Challenges and blockers

- The first round-2 edit introduced a regression. A `null` argument to the close
  path still resolved to the pill, which would have stolen focus from the task
  drawer. The explicit `restoreFocus` flag replaces that argument and removes
  the ambiguity.
- Three palette tests still read the listbox from the scroll wrapper after the
  restructure. They now query `[role='listbox']`.
- The shot schema has no viewport field, so the declared palette screenshot
  cannot pin 375px. The WebKit fixture suite remains the three-width evidence.
- The two read-only `docs/qa/*` records are still locked. Their palette copy is
  stale until someone with write access unlocks them.

## Key learnings

- A shared component needs its fallback and ARIA wiring in the component, not in
  each caller. The round-1 review found sibling instances of the same invalid
  child, which is the reason for fixing the class rather than the one element.
- Use the combobox definition of expanded that matches what is actually rendered.
  Binding it to the overlay's open state would announce "expanded" over an empty
  popup.
- A nullable argument that means "restore" in one branch and "no restore" in
  another is easy to get wrong. An explicit flag reads better.
